title: Underwater Choreography Director
description: The user directs an underwater animation sequence where Kira, a robot, and a school of BarramundiFish perform synchronized choreography along a timeline. Users assign keyframed motion paths, adjust timing curves, and manage energy conservation across performers — each animation transfer must preserve total kinetic energy. Full undo/redo support lets users refine the performance.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an underwater choreography director. Load BarramundiFish.glb, kira.glb, and robot.glb from the shared_assets folder using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: underwater environment with blue-green fog, caustic-style animated point lights, a sandy plane floor, and subtle particle bubbles. Place Kira center-left, the robot center-right, and three cloned BarramundiFish swimming in a loose arc above them. Camera: perspective at 60 FOV, OrbitControls enabled, initial position (0,3,10) looking at origin. Core mechanic — Energy-Conserved Animation Transfer: maintain a global kinetic energy pool (starts at 100 units). A bottom timeline bar (HTML/CSS overlay) shows 10 seconds divided into 0.5s slots. Users click a character to select it (highlight with emissive outline), then click a timeline slot to place a keyframe. Each keyframe opens a small panel to set motion type (spin, bounce, swim-wave, slide) and intensity (1-5). Intensity costs energy: intensity × 5 units deducted from the pool. Removing a keyframe refunds energy. The pool display updates in real time — users cannot exceed 100 total energy (conservation law). Multi-input coupling: holding Shift while placing a keyframe links two selected characters so they mirror or complement each other's motion in that slot (coupled pair costs 1.5× single energy). A Play button interpolates all keyframes using THREE.AnimationMixer with custom KeyframeTrack curves, blending between idle poses and assigned motions. Implement full undo/redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) using a command stack that records every keyframe add, remove, or coupling action and properly restores energy. Show energy bar, undo/redo buttons, and timeline as HTML overlays. Ensure at least 10-14 distinct interaction steps are needed to fill a compelling choreography across all five characters.
